newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean lawmakers demand end to censorship.
newsitem.headline: Chilean lawmakers demand end to censorship.

text.p: Chilean lawmakers on on Thursday demanded an end to "cultural authoritarianism" after a television station was threatened with sanctions for jokes about the Bible and the national flag.
"What is clear is that in our country cultural authoritarianism still lingers on," socialist Sen. Ricardo Nunez told reporters.
"Part of the discussion is how to eliminate authoritarianism in Chile not only in the political sense and in values, but fundamentally in culture."

The sanctions against the Rock and Pop television channel revived a debate over censorship that started last month when the Supreme Court upheld a ban on Martin Scorsese's film, "The Last Temptation of Christ."
Chile has some of the strictest censorship laws in Latin America, a legacy of Gen. Augusto Pinochet's military regime, which ruled with an iron grip from 1973 to 1990.
The Rock and Pop channel was taken to task for a comedy programme that parodied the Bible, made jokes about the national anthem and portrayed Barbie dolls as transvestites.

"Every democratic society must guarantee (an outlet for) people's sense of humour and allow a certain space for irreverence," said socialist Sen. Carlos Ominami. "Any country which loses this, risks returning to authoritarianism."
The government has sent a law to Congress to end film and television censorship, creating in its place a classification system.
